summary: The app runs as a coherent balcony sun-study tool: a furnished, orbitable 3D balcony with wall, railing and overhang shadows; sample location, date, orientation and daylight controls; draggable top-view planters; and a same-time split comparison of two arrangements. Desktop and mobile layouts remained usable, and the documented NOAA approximation made the simplified model clear.

runtime.reason: The page loaded and remained interactive before and after reload. The root, stylesheet, app module and Three.js resources returned successfully; the only console error was a nonblocking missing favicon.ico.

scene.reason: The scene is genuine, camera-interactive 3D rather than a static image: orbiting and pitching the camera produced consistent parallax, occlusion and perspective changes across the balcony, furniture, railing and overhang.

checks.reason: Three materially different camera views showed correct depth and spatial relationships: the exterior overview, a rotated side view, and a high-angle view where the roof/overhang occludes the interior.
Composition, type, muted palette, plan graphics and stylized 3D form a coherent identity. Important readouts, planter states and controls remain legible on desktop and mobile.

The primary controls produced meaningful feedback: location/date changes updated solar values, heading changes updated the compass and model, and daylight scrubbing changed both the 3D lighting and planter sun/shade results.

Repeated A/B switching, same-time comparison, time reversal and returning to the edited A plan all worked. Slider keyboard Home/End boundary checks and a full page reload also succeeded; the devoted Reset layout recovery control is present.

Desktop 1440x900 and mobile 390x844 layouts were usable. The mobile full-page capture shows all lower controls and assumptions reachable within the 390px column, and reload restored a stable initial state. Actual touch hardware was not assessed.
The furnished balcony has a solid side wall, metal railing and deep overhang. Low-sun and alternate-angle views show geometrically plausible railing, wall, planter and overhang shadows and occlusion.

Sydney and 2026-12-21 replaced the defaults; the local time, solar altitude/azimuth and planter statuses updated. Heading changed from 218° to 203°, and scrubbing from 05:41 to 20:05 changed lighting and totals from 0/5 to 5/5 in sun.
Dragging planter 03 in the top view moved its numbered marker and 3D position. At 12:25 it changed to Shade, the list updated, and the plan count fell to 3/5 in sun.

Plan A and Plan B were separately editable and then shown side by side at the same 12:25 time. Their planter positions differ, and at 10:35 both comparison panels updated together while showing different 3/5 and 2/5 shade counts.

Eight bundled sample cities were immediately selectable without location permission or an API key. The visible model panel discloses the clear-sky NOAA approximation, its latitude/longitude/local-time inputs, unmodelled terrain/buildings/clouds/reflection, and ray-tested shadow assumptions.

instruction.reason: Every stated requirement was delivered and worked together across the tested states: furnished shadow-casting balcony, environmental controls, daylight scrubbing, top-view editing, same-time A/B comparison, and disclosed sample-based solar assumptions.

spatial.reason: Geometry, camera depth, occlusion and shadow direction remain coherent across overview, side and high-angle views. Furniture and planters are spatially grounded, and the wall, railing and overhang visibly shape the light.

interaction.reason: Primary operations, combinations, repeated plan switching and reversal behaved reliably with clear immediate feedback. The draggable plan and split comparison naturally support the planning task.

visual.reason: The warm material palette, restrained typography, legible overlays and consistent plan/readout styling create a purposeful sun-study expression rather than unrelated decoration.

stability.reason: Desktop, mobile, repeated edits, comparison, time reversal and reload remained stable and readable. All required resources loaded; the sole console error was an irrelevant favicon 404.

limitations: The console contained one nonblocking error: favicon.ico returned 404. All stylesheet, app and Three.js requests succeeded (console.txt and network.txt).

At the tested solar boundary, both 05:41 and 20:05 reported altitude -1 degrees but produced different results (0/5 in sun versus 5/5 in sun). This appears to be a simplified-model edge behavior; the solar assumptions are disclosed and the required daylight flow still updates consistently.
Actual touch hardware, audio quality, downloaded exports and other internal implementation details were not applicable or verifiable; no export control was observed.
